question: What is the shape of the pelvic inlet in an anthropoid pelvis?

options.A: A wide oval from side to side
options.D: A long oval from front to back

explanation: The anthropoid pelvis is shaped like an oval where the front-to-back measurement is longer than the side-to-side measurement. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why does a midwife need to identify an anthropoid pelvis during pregnancy?

options.A: To know if the mother needs a blood transfusion
options.C: To figure out the exact gestational age of the fetus
options.D: To understand how the baby will move through the birth canal

explanation: Knowing the pelvic shape helps midwives anticipate how labor will progress and spot any mechanical challenges early. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which bone feature is commonly found in an anthropoid pelvis?

options.B: A side-to-side inlet wider than the front-to-back
options.D: A short sacrum with four segments

explanation: The anthropoid pelvis typically features prominent ischial spines that can narrow the middle part of the pelvic cavity. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h2)

question: How does the sacrum usually look in an anthropoid pelvis?
explanation: The sacrum in this pelvic type is long and narrow, which makes the pelvic cavity deeper from front to back. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which pelvic measurement is longer at the inlet of an anthropoid pelvis?
explanation: The main feature of the anthropoid inlet is a front-to-back diameter that is longer than the side-to-side diameter. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h3)

question: A woman with an anthropoid pelvis has a narrow side-to-side inlet. How does the baby's head usually enter the pelvis?

options.A: The baby stays floating until the last stage of labor
options.D: Engagement happens above the brim without any alignment

explanation: Because side-to-side space is limited, the fetal head enters the pelvis aligned with the long front-to-back path. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which fetal position is more common in an anthropoid pelvis than in a standard round pelvis?
explanation: The narrow shape of the anthropoid pelvis means babies are found in the occipitoposterior position much more often during labor. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is a common effect of narrow side-to-side dimensions during labor?

options.A: The baby travels down in a front-to-back alignment
options.C: A rapid birth without any skull molding
options.D: The shoulders come out before the head

explanation: The restricted side-to-side room forces the fetus to travel down the birth canal using the long front-to-back axis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is a patient, watchful approach recommended during the second stage of labor in an anthropoid pelvis?

options.A: The placenta separates too early in this pelvis type
options.C: Oxytocin drips are banned for first-time mothers
options.D: Labor can take longer due to the deep cavity and posterior positions

explanation: A deeper pelvis and posterior positions require extra time for the baby to descend, so patience prevents unnecessary medical interventions. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe first step when managing a posterior baby position in an anthropoid pelvis?

options.A: Monitoring the baby's heart rate closely
options.B: Using a vacuum extractor before the cervix is fully open
options.C: Encouraging the mother to change positions

explanation: Instrumental delivery is never performed before the cervix is fully dilated, regardless of the shape of the pelvis. [learn more](BMP210_U1_T5#BMP210_U1_T5_h5)
